title: Book of Lives: A Memoir of Sorts

vibeProfile.oneLine: Atwood turns her wit on her own long, remarkable life.

summary: Late in a remarkable life, Margaret Atwood turns her wit and clear eye on her own story, from a bush childhood in the Canadian wilderness to a career at the centre of world literature, and the losses and loves along the way. Called a memoir 'of sorts' because Atwood distrusts tidy life stories, it is candid, funny and characteristically sceptical of its own genre. A generous, unsentimental self-portrait from one of the defining writers of the age.
whyReadIt: Atwood's own life, told with the wit and scepticism she brings to everything. Candid, funny and unsentimental.

funFacts.text: Atwood has often resisted straightforward autobiography, hence the wry subtitle 'a memoir of sorts'.
